purpose: OPERATOR REFERENCE ONLY — never design DNA. The owl template is the sole source of design and structure.
strengths: Genuine trust stack is already assembled: Owens Corning Preferred Contractor, HomeAdvisor Screened & Approved, Angi A rating, BBB A+, Google 5.0 — real, verifiable badges most competitors do not have.
Three real named testimonials with towns are placed high on the homepage.
Services are clear and correctly scoped to roofing, siding, gutters.
The quote form already segments by job type (Roof Repair, Roof Replace, Siding, Gutters, Storm Damage) and captures address — good lead qualification intent.
Both the PA and MD offices are published with separate phone numbers.
weaknesses: No above-the-fold value proposition beyond a generic tagline. The hero says what they do, never why to choose them — the callback/reliability angle that their own reviews prove is absent.
Overlapping icon nav strip collides with its own labels ('AREAS WE SER...' is clipped by the overlapping badge), a layout defect visible at 1280px.
A stray Pink Panther graphic sits inside the SERVICES header band next to the Owens Corning badge — off-brand and undermines the credibility the badge is there to build.
Service cards use white body text on a saturated red panel at small size — fails contrast comfort and is hard to read.
Badge row is horizontally clipped at 1280px; the HomeAdvisor and Google badges are cut off at both edges.
No dedicated service-area pages. Counties are listed as a run-on paragraph inside the About block, which is unusable for local SEO across two states.
No individual service detail depth on the homepage; roofing/siding/gutters each get two sentences and a Learn More.
Privacy Policy and Terms of Service link off-site to thebasalygagroup.com — a third-party domain, not the client's own legal pages.
Phone inconsistency: the footer displays (877) 570-3774 while the tel: link behind it dials 570-382-8629.
No accessibility affordances visible (no cookie/consent control, no visible skip nav), and the Wix build ships heavy client-side JS.
No storm-damage or insurance-claim page despite storm damage being an option in their own quote form and a major theme in their reviews.
Project gallery exists but is not surfaced with location or job detail on the homepage, so the strongest local proof stays buried.
load_notes: Wix-hosted, image-heavy, full-page height ~4280px at 1280px viewport. Screenshot captured cleanly with no WAF interception.
